facts.text: Riverhills received its official name in 1973, chosen by the Queensland Place Names Board after a developer suggested a title reflecting the area's geography.
The suburb climbs from just 10 metres beside the Brisbane River to over 40 metres on the northern bank of Wolston Creek, giving it a distinctly hilly feel.
Riverhills is part of Brisbane’s Centenary Suburbs, a development that began in 1959 under the Hooker Centenary Project.
Newcomb Park on Sumners Road hosts a boat launching area where residents can take non‑motorised craft out onto the Brisbane River.
From that same park, the Centenary Rowing Club and Lakers Dragon Boat Club offer rowing and dragon boat experiences to locals and visitors alike.
Riverhills Plaza, located on Bogong Street, serves as the suburb’s main shopping hub.
